messages:
marek: quick check - ran a dry-run for hourly aggregates (partial hours) and preview shows oddly high delta in a couple shards

sophia: drop the command + preview payload?

marek: `POST /v1/recompute/preview 
{ 
  \"job\": \"hourly_agg\", 
  \"start\": \"2026-03-01T08:00:00Z\", 
  \"end\": \"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z\", 
  \"shards\": [7,8], 
  \"mode\": \"partial\" 
}`

leah: did preview include the cache-prefetch overlap model? if cached prefixes are applied to hours overlap, the preview might double-count

olivia: preview currently simulates applied deltas + prefix merge. We try to de-dupe but our simulator uses window boundaries from request only, not last_committed_window

jason: that's the bug. Preview must consult last_committed_window per shard so users see non-overlapping deltas

kevin: infra proposal: preview endpoint does two passes - 1) query committed_watermarks for requested shards 2) compute effective_windows = intersection(request_window, >watermark) and return estimations for those windows only

marek: agree. Also we need to surface routing and quota effects in preview. Product wants \"estimate runtime + cost + infra impact\"

sophia: UX sketch: preview returns {affected_shards, estimated_rows, estimated_compute_units, estimated_cost, infra_impact_note}. Show a visual Heatmap for shards so user can toggle to exclude hot shards

leah: toggle to exclude is great. But we should default to not touching hot shards unless user explicitly allows it (checkbox: \"allow high-heat shards (may increase cost)\") :warning:

jason: from writer side ensure idempotency: upsert semantics with `dedupe_key=(agg_key, window_start)` + `commit_id`. If preview vs real run disagree, capture telemetry to reconcile.

kevin: routing: recompute traffic should prefer `backfill-lowprio` pool. Add per-org concurrent backfill limit and global circuit breaker. If queue_depth > 500, throttle and surface a message in console: \"Backfill load high - expected delay\"

olivia: console prototype will show three columns: Preview (estimates), Shard heatmap (toggle), Routing & ETA (pool, queue depth, estimated start)

marek: what about materialized views? Data platform: if we run large partials they may invalidate MV TTLs leading to noisy reads for 24h after backfill
\
data-platform: correct - we should bump MV refresh windows before big recomputes or set read-consistency header on downstream queries. Suggest small preflight: `POST /v1/recompute/preflight` that returns MV conflicts and suggests extending TTLs

kevin: I'll add `preflight` step to the pipeline and make preview call it automatically for runs above N shards or M estimated_rows

leah: telemetry: add metrics `recompute.preview` (tags: mode, shards_count, exclude_hot_shards), `recompute.submitted`, `recompute.queued_delay_ms`, and histogram for `recompute.actual_cost_vs_preview_ratio`

jason: test plan: integration test that calls preview, then submit run with injected flakiness and assert final aggregates match preview-normalized results when last_committed_window is honored

marek: small note for console copy: show a micro copy line: \"Preview uses latest committed watermarks to estimate net delta; final results may differ if new events arrive after preview.\" Keep it simple

olivia: will mock UI strings. Also adding small affordance: \"Schedule run\" vs \"Run now\" - scheduled runs inherit a backfill window that avoids peak hours

kevin: policy: scheduled backfills default to off-peak hour routing and lower concurrency. Immediate runs need explicit \"Use high-priority pool\" checkbox and org-admin permission

engbot: build 5892 queued by kevin for branch recompute-preflight (CI will run idempotency test)

marek: OK next steps I hear: 1) implement watermark consult in preview + preflight hooks (infra) 2) add preflight MV checks (data-platform) 3) console preview UI + toggle to exclude hot shards (olivia) 4) telemetry + tests (jason/kevin) 5) pricing copy + confirm with finance (sophia)

leah: tagging owners in cards now. I'll run a couple of manual dry-runs on staging tonight and post diffs tomorrow morning :coffee:

marek: thanks. If preview still spikes numbers, we should block submit with a soft-fail and require explicit override

sophia: agreed - soft-fail with override checkbox and audit log entry (who overrode + reason)
